title: Rock arrives and the hit-and-miss years
summary: He leads many bands and works with others through the late 1950s to early 1970s, when rock made jobs harder to find.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: And, he began what turned out to be about 15 years or more of constant touring all around this country and all around Europe and, uh, do you want to start talking about that or do you want to wait---

WELL, God - it's going to take 45 hours of tape to do all these things, but to make a long story short in this period, I had many bands and I worked with many bands - not as a leader, but I worked with many groups that had jobs and I took jobs--
You were the leader of many.
Many as the leader and, you know, Rock had come in and really hit it in the pit of the stomach and, uh, I must say that I had some very hard times - I

managed to keep going - I managed to keep going okay but it wasn't like it was in the old days; it just had changed and it was harder - and it was harder to find places to play and those were kind of bad times in there and that continued on; it hit and miss, you know, just kept going but I wouldn't stop playing for anything and I went right on doing it.
And, you always managed to make a living---
Oh, I always managed to do that-- yeah.
And, sometimes it was pretty good and sometimes it was pretty dry--
This was all through the late '50's -- all through the '60's and, then, into the early '70's.
Yeah. It was a hit and miss proposition; it was--- you'd be rich one day and a pauper the next. You know, it's just one of those things.
